name: Dunsan
tagline: The planned business district, wide streets and government offices
description: Daejeon's modern core, laid out on a grid west of the old centre to hold the government complex, the arts centre and the city's main commercial district. Wide boulevards, department stores, the best restaurants and a large park make this the most comfortable part of the city to live in.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the restaurants, the arts centre and the metro on a walkable grid
pros: The best restaurants, shopping and cafes in Daejeon
Metro line and buses in every direction
Expo park and green space nearby
cons: The highest rents in the city
Planned and corporate rather than characterful
Busy with office traffic on weekdays

name: Yuseong
tagline: Hot springs, KAIST and the research institutes
description: The northwestern district holding KAIST, the Daedeok research cluster and a long-established hot spring quarter with public baths and hotels. It has the highest concentration of international researchers in Korea outside Seoul, which makes it the most navigable district for a foreigner.
bestFor: Anyone connected to KAIST or the research institutes, with the baths as a bonus
pros: KAIST and the research cluster on the doorstep
Public hot spring baths in the district
The most English-friendly part of the city
cons: Twenty minutes by metro to Dunsan

name: Jung-gu and Eunhaeng-dong
tagline: The old downtown near the station, cheapest and most lived-in
description: The original city centre around Daejeon station, with the old market, the Eunhaeng-dong pedestrian streets and Sungsimdang, the bakery people travel across the country for. It is older and scruffier than Dunsan, and the rents are the lowest anywhere central.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting the KTX station, the market and the famous bakery close by
pros: KTX to Seoul in under an hour from the station
The lowest central rents in the city
Traditional market and the best street food
cons: Visibly older and less well kept than Dunsan
Some streets around the station are uncomfortable late

name: Gung-dong and the University Belt
tagline: Student streets between Chungnam National University and KAIST
description: The area between the two big campuses, full of cheap restaurants, bars, noraebang and one-room studios aimed at students. It has the liveliest night scene in Daejeon and by some distance the cheapest short-term housing, at the cost of being loud on term-time evenings.
bestFor: Cheap long stays with the university nightlife on the doorstep
pros: The cheapest studios in the city
Dense cheap eating and student nightlife
Walking distance to both major campuses
cons: Loud on weekday and weekend nights

name: Gyeryongsan Edge and Doan
tagline: New apartment towers with the national park behind
description: The southwestern expansion of the city, where new high-rise apartment complexes have gone up against the edge of Gyeryongsan National Park. Modern flats, good schools and supermarkets, with mountain trails starting a short bus ride away and the metro extension reaching the district.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a modern flat with the national park close
pros: Newest and best-equipped apartments in the city
Gyeryongsan trails a short ride away
cons: Twenty-five minutes from the old downtown
